newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra sees federal-state deficits fading.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra sees federal-state deficits fading.

text.p: The Australian Treasury on Friday projected the disappearance of combined federal and state general-government deficits in the year to June 2000.
"The achievement of underlying surplus in 1999-00 will move the combined sector into a net lending posiiton for the first time since 1989-90," the Treasury said in its annual National Fiscal Outlook.

The Treasury projected that the combined general government balance -- slightly different from budget balances -- would become a A$4.6 billion surplus in 1999/00, compared with the A$8.8 billion deficit in the current fiscal year.

"The improvement arises from fiscal consolidation measures undertaken by the Commonwealth (federal government) in the 1996/97 budget in conjunction with continuing underlying surpluses in the aggregate state and territory sector," it said.

"It does not incorporate assumptions in respect of the statement by the Commonwealth government, at the time of its Mid-year Economic and Fiscal Outlook, that additional fiscal tightening (will) be necessary."

Treasurer Peter Costello has said the government will tighten its finances in the May budget by A$2 billion to A$4 billion, compared with the A$7 billion tightening effected last year. The general government balance has a slightly wider coverage than the budget by including the transactions of some non-core government operations.
It does not, however, include trading enterprises.

The Treasury produces these estimates each year as a basis for negotiations at the annual Premiers Conference and Loans Council meetings, in which the federal and state governments hammer out their financial relations for the coming year.
